Wendy Bianchi [10:11 A.M.]: So which figure do I use? The cold room and the kitchen sheets are set for sixty, and our accounts office bills from this record.

Wendy Bianchi [10:14 A.M.]: Can I release the order on that?

From: Gerald Ibarra
Date: March 2
Subject: Fair contacts and follow-up order
Dear Claudia,
We came back from the two-day housewares fair at the Kelso exhibition center on Tuesday evening with forty-eight new contacts, the largest number any of our staff has brought back from a single event. The crates of display units traveled home on the same truck and have already been unpacked in the storeroom. Our second production run of the lidded pantry containers is due to be completed on March 14, and shipments to distributors begin in that same week.
Only twelve demonstration units remain in the storeroom, and because one unit must be left with a customer at each first visit, the order in which we approach these contacts has to be fixed before the first calls are made. Even so, a contact list that long means the trip paid for itself.

2. Regional distributors who took a catalog but gave no order estimate. Reach these second and ask how many units each of them would expect to take. The customer service desk is still logging inquiries from the fair, so keep your notes separate from theirs.
3. Independent gift shops. Write to these only after the distributors have replied and it is clear that demonstration units are still uncommitted.
Once all twelve units have been committed, place any remaining contacts on a hold list and tell them that a visit can be arranged as soon as the new units reach us.
Thank you,
Gerald Ibarra

To: All installation crews
From: Helen Mortimer, Fitting Supervisor
Date: February 27
Subject: Completion images and billing
From Monday, March 6, closing out a job will include one new step: photographing the finished work at the customer's home and sending the images to the office.
Why this is changing.
Over the past four months several accounts have gone unpaid for weeks because customers questioned marks and missing pieces that we could not account for once the crew had left. Some of you have called this extra paperwork at the end of a long day, and I understand that, but we have nothing to show what we handed over. Every van already carries a tablet, so no new equipment is needed.
Each set must show the following:
[1] the whole run of units with every door and drawer closed
[2] the joint where the counter meets the wall
[3] the toe boards along the floor
[4] the inside of one upper unit with its shelves in place
[5] the floor and walls beside the finished units
On jobs of more than twelve units, add a wide view from the opposite corner. A sample set has already been circulated to crew leaders.
The images must be uploaded before the van comes back in. The office cannot release the bill for a job until the record is on file, so a set that arrives the next morning holds up payment. Staff here will match each set to the invoice.
Who is covered now.
For the next four weeks the step applies only to the three crews at the north yard, where Culver Timber Supply will keep delivering materials to each address as before. Crew leaders in that group will check every set before it is sent. When the four weeks are up, the remaining crews will hear from me about a short training session. If customers continue to raise questions after that, we may ask for a signature on site as well.
This notice is posted in the tool room. Each crew leader must add initials beside the crew number.

Result.
The spring catalog mailing was finished on March 6, and all 12,400 pieces were entered into the postal stream that day. Since then, 187 pieces have come back to our plant as undeliverable. Reasons for return.

Submitting the request.
Corrected records contain your customers' personal details, so the resubmission form may be filed only by a member of your staff who has completed our data handling briefing and has been issued a briefing reference number. To: Ms. Fiona Steadman
From: Gavin Lindqvist
Sent: February 27, 10:12 A.M.
Subject: Energy review — site screening (WR-118)
Copy: Site Services file
Dear Ms. Steadman,
Brackenridge Energy Services reviews one property per company in each intake, so only one site can be entered this round.
I have checked our four premises against the published conditions. Gas and electricity at Netherby Road reach us through the landlord's service charge, as they have since we took that unit. Bramley Lane is metered in our own name, though we moved in last April. Vine Street has had its own meters for years, but the building returns to its owner in September. Torrance Park has been ours since 2016, its meters are in our name, and the lease there runs to 2032.
The entry form calls for twelve months of meter readings. For the site I have in mind, the earlier readings sit with our former billing agent, and the March cutoff is one week away. I would therefore aim at the following intake. Should the optional action plan be included?
Gavin Lindqvist
Facilities Coordinator, Site Services
Talbot Packaging
Extension 2140
----------------------
From: Fiona Steadman
Date: February 27, 1:45 P.M.
To: Gavin Lindqvist
Subject: Re: Energy review — site screening (WR-118)
File the entry against the March cutoff, not the later one. Our annual stock count runs at Vine Street through June and will occupy this department, so the survey should be finished before it begins. Telephone the former billing agent's accounts desk for the readings, which is quicker than writing.
This year's facilities budget carries nothing for outside consultancy fees, so keep us to what the program provides. Once the entry has gone in, obtain written confirmation that our place is held.
F. S.
For internal circulation only.
